quote: Theorem 3.10.1 Let X ~ PEL(v1, q1, alpha1) and Y ~ PEL(v2, q2, alpha2) if v1 <= v2, q1 <= q2 and alpha1 <= alpha2, we have Y >=lr X then Y >=hr X, Y >=mrl X and Y >=st X.
family: PEL(v, q, alpha): power exponentiated Lindley, cdf F(x) = [v^{{1 - e^{-qx}(1+q+qx)/(1+q)}^alpha} - 1]/(v-1), x > 0, alpha > 0, q > 0, v > 0, v != 1
compared: two PEL random variables with componentwise ordered parameters (v1,q1,alpha1) <= (v2,q2,alpha2)

hypotheses.text: v1 <= v2, q1 <= q2 and alpha1 <= alpha2
hypotheses.formal: componentwise ordering of all three parameters

conclusion.direction: Y >=_lr X (hence Y >=_hr X, Y >=_mrl X, Y >=_st X)

ambiguity: Statement reads 'if v1 <= v2, q1 <= q2 and alpha1 <= alpha2, we have Y >=lr X then Y >=hr X...'; whether Y >=lr X is a hypothesis or the proved conclusion is grammatically ambiguous, but the proof establishes lr (derivative of f_X/f_Y negative, verified graphically via Figure 10 rather than analytically).
